sentences.text:
On behalf of Respondent No.1 - Insurance Company Shri Sant
Divisional Branch Manager, Oriental Insurance Company, Indore is presnet along with Shri Sudhir
V. Dandwate - Advocate.

Award  This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking appropriate compensation amount by setting aside dismissal of his claim by learned Sixth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Indore, District Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.64 of 2014 decided on 25.08.2015.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Indore, District Indore (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Today the appeal is listed before the Permanent & Continuous/ National Lok Adalat under Section 20 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 for settlement between the parties.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant - claimant submits that the claim of the claimant has been dismissed by the learned Claims Tribunal solely on the ground that the appellant was a driver of vehicle bearing registration number MP-19 EA-0153.

On 25.02.2010, this appellant was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6265 2 MA-1762-2015 driving the aforesaid vehicle from Indore to Mhow and when the bus reached in front of Phalbagh, AB Road, Indore, District Indore (MP), a truck bearing registration number MP-09 KA-4254 dashed the bus; and on account of accident, he sustained injuries on various parts and was admitted in MY Hospital, Indore.

Thereafter, he was shifted to various private hospitals for treatment; and incurred a total amount of Mukesh vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 8 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132529666/
1 Rs.2,00,000/- (rupees two lakhs only) expenses for the treatment.

entities.text: Mukesh vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to him, he suffered disablement and thereafter, he is not in a position to drive the vehicle.

3. Respondent No.2 - owner remained ex parte and the claim case was contested by respondent No.1 - Insurance Company by taking a defense that the claimant was not having a valid driving licence on the date of accident.
There was no fitness certificate of the vehicle and due to violation of condition of the policy, the claim is liable to be dismissed.

4. Learned Claims Tribunal framed five issues for adjudication; while answering Issue No.1, the accident was found proved; while answering Issue No.2, 15% permanent disablement was found;
however, while answering Issue No.4, the Tribunal has held that since he (claimant) himself was the driver of the vehicle, therefore, he is not entitled for compensation.

In light of judgment delivered by the the larger bench of the Apex Court in case of United India Insurance Company Limited v. Sunil Kumar & others reported in (2019) 12 SCC 398 , which overruled the law laid down by the Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Sinitha and others reported in (2012) ACJ 1 = (2012) 2 SCC 356 .

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited v. Sunil Kumar & others reported in (2019) 12 SCC 398
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Sinitha and others reported in (2012) ACJ 1 = (2012) 2 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now, the claim by a driver of the offending vehicle under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6265 3 MA-1762-2015 is maintainable, even if he himself is negligent.

5. In view of the above, we have discussed this matter in Lok Adalat in presence of the appellant - claimant and Shri Santosh Patel, Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited, Indore and their respective counsel.

6. After discussion and hearing learned counsel appearing for both parties and after perusing the relevant record, we are of the opinion that impugned order dated 25.08.2015 passed Claim Case No.64 of 2014 by the learned Sixth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore deserves to be and is hereby set aside; and the claimant deserves to be compensated with an appropriate amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only).
We, therefore, suggest the parties that the matter may be settled on these lines.
7. Accepting our suggestion, the parties have entered into a settlement.
Learned counsel for the parties submit that this appeal can be disposed of in view of the settlement arrived at between the parties.
Learned counsel appearing for respondent/Insurance Company submits that the Insurance Company has agreed to pay Rs.2,00,000/- as full and final settlement against his claim.
An application / docket to that effect, which has been signed by learned counsel for both the parties, has been filed.
The compromise between the parties is verified.
It is just, valid and lawful.

It is,
therefore, ordered to be recorded.

8. Accordingly, an award is passed in the following terms: -
(a) That Respondent-Insurance Company shall pay a total sum of Rs.2,00,000/-
without interest, as full and final satisfaction of the claim made by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6265 4 MA-1762-2015 the appellant in this appeal.

Mukesh vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 8 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132529666/
2 (b) That Respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the aforesaid amount in the Claims Tribunal for payment to the appellant within a period of three months from today, failing which this additional amount shall be recoverable with interest calculated at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of this award.

entities.text: Mukesh vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 8 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (c) On deposit being made, Claims Tribunal shall permit appellant to withdraw the same.

(d) Since the matter has been settled between the parties in this National Lok Adalat, the Court fees,
if any, paid by the claimant(s) be refunded on issuing certificate by the Registry.
(e) This appeal is finally disposed of and the parties to bear their own costs.
(f) The copy of the application filed by the parties be kept in the record of this appeal.
(g) Copy of the award be given to both the parties free of charges.
(JUSTICE VIVEK RUSIA)
